app.title: TraceChain - A supply-chain traceability blockchain simulation
app.subtitle: Follow a batch of coffee from the growing region to the consumer
app.simulationNotice: This is a simulated blockchain environment for learning. It is not connected to any real blockchain network.
app.permissionedNotice: The model simulated here is a permissioned blockchain: only recognized organizations can write transactions.
start.heading: Start the activity
start.objectivesHeading: After this activity you will be able to
start.objective1: Explain how a physical batch is represented as a digital asset on the ledger
start.objective3: Distinguish current state from transaction history
start.objective4: Explain why a committed record is corrected rather than deleted
start.objective5: Determine recall scope from provenance relationships
start.objective6: State the limits of blockchain regarding the truthfulness of input data
start.restartConfirmBody: All progress and scores from your previous session will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
status.standalone: Standalone mode: progress is being saved in this browser and has not been sent to Moodle.
stage.orientation.title: Step 1 - Meet the simulated blockchain network
stage.orientation.instruction: Before writing anything to the ledger, look at the real supply chain and the organizations in it. The coffee batch is a physical object; the ledger record is only a digital representation of it.
stage.orientation.supplyChainAlt: Supply chain diagram: producer co-operative, certification body, logistics provider, processing plant, distributor, retailer, consumer and regulator.
stage.orientation.checkQuestion: Does blockchain automatically prove that the original data is true?
stage.orientation.checkOptionYes: Yes. Once data is on a blockchain it is certainly true.
stage.orientation.checkOptionNo: No. Blockchain helps establish who wrote the data and whether it has changed, but it does not prove the data is true.
stage.orientation.checkOptionPartly: Yes, if the transaction is endorsed by several organizations.
stage.orientation.checkFeedback: Blockchain can help establish who recorded data, when it was recorded, and whether it has been altered; but the truthfulness of the input still has to be verified by procedures, inspections, and the accountability of the participating organizations.
stage.orientation.noPenaltyNotice: This question is not scored. It is here so you can check your own starting assumptions.
stage.createBatch.title: Step 2 - Create the coffee batch on the ledger
stage.createBatch.instruction: You are the production manager at the co-operative. Create the first record for the green coffee batch just harvested. This will be the first transaction, and it will be written into the first block of the ledger.
stage.createBatch.sealBlock: Write the transaction into a block
stage.createBatch.sealBlockHelp: In a real blockchain a block may contain many transactions. Here we write it immediately so you can watch the first block form.
stage.anchorCertificate.title: Step 3 - Anchor the quality certificate
stage.shipAndMonitor.title: Step 4 - Hand over and monitor transport
stage.receiveAndCorrect.title: Step 5 - Receive the batch and correct the error
stage.transformBatch.title: Step 6 - Transform green coffee into roasted coffee
stage.packageAndDistribute.title: Step 7 - Package and distribute the finished product
stage.verifyAndTamper.title: Step 8 - Verify provenance and attempt tampering
stage.recallAndDebrief.title: Step 9 - Trace and recall the product

endorsement.notice: In a real network each organization endorses using its own system. Here the system endorses on behalf of the other parties so that you can work through this alone.
validation.heading: Business rule check results
validation.someFailed: The transaction was not accepted. Review the unsatisfied rules below.
validation.actorAuthorized: The actor is authorized to submit this transaction.
validation.actorNotAuthorized: The actor is not authorized to submit transactions on this network.
validation.organizationUnknown: The submitting organization is not among the recognized organizations.
validation.actionNotPermitted: This organization is not permitted to perform the selected action.
validation.producerMismatch: The batch must be created by the same organization that is submitting the transaction.
validation.organizationInactive: The organization is no longer active on this network.
validation.assetIdUnique: The batch identifier has not been used before.
validation.assetIdAlreadyExists: This batch identifier already exists on the ledger. Each batch needs its own identifier.
validation.quantityMustBePositive: The quantity must be greater than 0.
validation.quantityNotANumber: The quantity must be a number.
validation.unitCompatible: The unit of measure is compatible.
validation.packageSizeRequired: When the unit is packages, declare the mass of each package so the system can compare masses.
validation.packageSizeNotApplicable: Only declare a package mass when the unit is packages.

message.inputTruth: Blockchain helps preserve and trace submitted records, but it does not automatically prove that a physical-world claim is true.
message.correction: Committed records are not edited or deleted. A new correction transaction is added and linked to the original record.
message.sharedLedger: A shared ledger does not necessarily mean that every participant can see every item of data.
message.blockchainNecessity: Blockchain is most defensible when independent organizations need shared records and do not want one participant to control the entire system.
message.physicalDigital: Reliable traceability also requires identifiers, procedures, sensors, inspections, authorized data sources, and organizational accountability.
message.tamperDetected: The hash chain is no longer consistent. Altering the old record has invalidated this block and every block after it.
